stories.title: European heatwave is most severe ever recorded - study
stories.summary: The record-shattering warmth in Europe in recent days is the most severe heatwave ever recorded in the region and is unequivocally the result of climate change driven by the burning of fossil fuels. That is the conclusion of a new rapid analysis of the heatwave conducted by World Weather Attribution climate scientists and published today. The report says June is now warming faster than any other month across Europe, and the high daytime and nighttime temperatures experienced over the past week would have been virtually impossible just a few decades ago. It says that if a similar heatwave had occurred in Europe 50 years ago, temperatures would have been about 3.5°C cooler.

stories.title: Thousands missing, 235 dead after Venezuela earthquakes
stories.summary: Hundreds of people in Venezuela were trapped under rubble and many more remained unaccounted for after two powerful earthquakes devastated areas in and around the capital Caracas, killing hundreds, damaging buildings and leaving thousands homeless. A magnitude 7.2 earthquake struck about ⁠160km west of Caracas on Wednesday evening, followed less than a minute later by a magnitude 7.5 tremor, the strongest since 1900, according to the US Geological Survey. The disaster hit a country already weakened by years of economic turmoil, which left much of its infrastructure fragile and complicated rescue efforts as aftershocks rattled the capital and surrounding coastal areas. Health Minister Carlos Alvarado said late yesterday that around 235 dead had been received by medical centres. He did not give a total number of casualties.

stories.title: Guerin family urges murderer to acknowledge his actions
stories.summary: A brother of Veronica Guerin has said that an apology from the man serving life in prison for her murder 30 years ago today would make a difference to the family. The 37-year-old journalist was shot dead in her car on the Naas Road in Dublin because she was prepared to give evidence against John Gilligan, the leader of a multimillion euro drugs gang, who assaulted her because of her work. Jimmy Guerin said the least the Parole Board should do before it releases Brian Meehan - who was convicted of the murder - is to look for an acknowledgment from him of the wrong he has done. The murder traumatised a family, shocked a nation and led to a realisation for the first time that, along with loyalist and republican terrorism, organised crime was a threat to the State and to the safety of citizens.

stories.title: Effects of Veronica Guerin's murder felt 30 years on
stories.summary: Sunday Independent journalist Veronica Guerin was murdered by a member of an organised crime gang on the Naas Road in Dublin 30 years ago today. In the years before her killing, she had been reporting on organised crime groups in Ireland, including John Gilligan's drugs empire. In life, Veronica faced down these gangs and reported on the realities of their actions, despite numerous threats and attacks. Her death led to widespread changes in how Ireland deals with organised crime and how journalists report on their activities.

stories.title: Thunderstorm warning for 16 counties as temperatures soar
stories.summary: A Status Yellow thunderstorm warning is in effect for several parts of the country as temperatures remain very high. The warning for Connacht, as well as counties Cavan, Donegal, Monaghan, Clare, Tipperary, Kildare, Laois, Longford, Meath, Offaly and Westmeath will remain in place until 6pm. Met Éireann is warning of localised flooding, difficult travelling conditions and possible damage to utilities including power, water, gas, and telecommunications. A high temperature warning for the entire country remains in place until 9am.

stories.title: Lopes hopes history repeats as Cape Verde face Saudis
stories.summary: Pico Lopes and his Cape Verde team-mates take the pitch in Houston tonight, aiming to overturn Saudi Arabia and reach the knockout stages at their first World Cup. But it is undeniable that the Shamrock Rovers' captain's World Cup odyssey has captured the imagination of the Irish public. After a magnificent 0-0 draw with Spain and a 1-1 tie against Uruguay, the African side will seal a place in the knockout stages with a draw or win against Saudi Arabia - just like it was 24 years ago in Japan when goals from Robbie Keane, Gary Breen and Damien Duff against the Arab nation secured Ireland's progress to the last 16 on the 2002 finals. In the build-up to the tournament, Lopes recalled the TV being wheeled into his Dublin classroom to watch that game in Yokohama - now it's his turn to face the Saudis with progress on the line.
